questions.question: What does cofactor expansion do to an $n\times n$ determinant?
options: It writes it as a sum involving smaller determinants.
It changes the matrix into a vector.
It turns it into a single matrix entry, under all circumstances whatsoever.
It replaces all entries by zeros.

questions.question: When expanding along row $i$, what is multiplied by the cofactor of entry $a_{ik}$?
options: The entry $a_{ik}$.
The determinant of the original matrix twice.
The column number $k$ alone.
The whole row $i$ as a vector.

questions.question: Cofactor expansion shows that the determinant of a triangular matrix equals:
options: the product of its diagonal entries
the sum of its diagonal entries
the product of all its entries
zero

questions.question: Why is a row with many zeros attractive for cofactor expansion?
options: Zeros turn the matrix into a non-square matrix.
Zeros make the determinant automatically equal to one.
Zeros remove all cofactor signs.
Zero entries make their expansion terms vanish.

questions.question: In cofactor expansion, the sign attached to entry $a_{ij}$ is:
options: always $+1$

questions.question: Expand along the first row of $\begin{pmatrix}2&0&0\\1&3&4\\5&6&7\end{pmatrix}$. What remains?
options: $2\det\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\5&6\end{pmatrix}$
$3\det\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\5&6\end{pmatrix}$
$2\det\begin{pmatrix}3&4\\6&7\end{pmatrix}$
$7\det\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&3\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: Compute $\det\begin{pmatrix}2&0&0\\1&3&4\\5&6&7\end{pmatrix}$ by expanding along the first row.
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\0&3&0\\4&0&5\end{pmatrix}$, which row or column is especially convenient for expansion?
options: No row or column can be used.
The third row.
The first column.
The second row.

questions.question: Compute $\det\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\0&3&0\\4&0&5\end{pmatrix}$ by expanding along the second row.
In expansion along row $1$, what is the sign of the term using $a_{12}$?
options: Undefined.
Positive.
Always zero.
Negative.

questions.question: Cofactor expansion along a row of all zeros gives a determinant of:
options: the product of the other rows
undefined

questions.question: What is the role of the deleted submatrix $A_{ik}$ in row expansion?
options: It decides which variable is free.
Its determinant gives the minor in the term for $a_{ik}$.
It gives the right-hand side vector.
It replaces the original matrix permanently.

questions.question: Why does cofactor expansion of a diagonal matrix lead to the product of diagonal entries?
options: At each expansion step, the off-diagonal zero terms vanish.
The determinant of every diagonal matrix is one.
Diagonal matrices have no minors.
Cofactor signs are all negative on the diagonal.

questions.question: Compute $\det\begin{pmatrix}4&0&0\\0&5&0\\0&0&6\end{pmatrix}$ using cofactor expansion.
Expand $\det\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\0&4&0\\5&6&7\end{pmatrix}$ along the second row. Which expression is correct?
options: $4\det\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\5&6\end{pmatrix}$
$-4\det\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\5&7\end{pmatrix}$
$4\det\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\5&7\end{pmatrix}$
$4\det\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\6&7\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: Compute $\det\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\0&4&0\\5&6&7\end{pmatrix}$ by expanding along the second row.
The cofactor sign follows a $(-1)^{i+j}$ checkerboard pattern. Which mistake ignores this pattern?
options: Using smaller determinants.
Choosing a row with zeros.
Treating every minor as if it had positive sign.
Expanding along a column instead of a row.

questions.question: Why can a row with many zeros be better than the first row even though both are valid?
options: It makes all cofactors equal to entries.
It changes the value of the determinant.
It avoids the need for square matrices.
It gives fewer nonzero terms to compute.

questions.question: Compute $\det\begin{pmatrix}0&2&0\\1&3&4\\0&5&0\end{pmatrix}$ by expanding along the first row.
A student expands along a row with entries $0,0,5$ and computes three $2\times2$ determinants. What should they notice?
options: All three minors must be added without signs, for every possible choice of input.
Expansion along that row is not allowed.
The determinant is automatically $5$.
Two of the three terms are multiplied by zero and need not be computed.
